key_insight: Thermal insulation can relax the need to suppress electron-to-lattice energy transfer, while absorber ohmic heat can be partially recycled into electrical work at the Carnot factor.
engineering_relevance: The analysis identifies absorber thermal insulation, electrical conductivity, and low contact-mediated heat leakage as design priorities for high-efficiency solar cells.
method: Thermodynamic analysis of nonideal hot-carrier and hot-absorber solar cells.
Accounting for finite absorber conductivity and ohmic heat recycling.
Sensitivity analysis of finite contact-mediated heat leakage.
evidence_signal: The abstract cites an 85.4% hot-carrier efficiency limit and reports thermodynamic analysis and heat-leakage sensitivity results, rather than experimental device validation.
watch_item: High efficiencies require ideal energy-selective contacts and negligible parasitic contact conductance; they are design targets, not practical efficiency projections.
paper_title: Nonideal Absorbers in Hot-Carrier and Hot-Absorber Solar Cells: Losses and Heat Recycling
